title: Samsung Plans to Bring More 2-Nanometer Chipmaking to Central Texas
gist: Samsung is advancing Taylor Fab 2 in Texas — construction targeted for November 2026, 2nm production, mass production in 2030 — within a $37B+ Central Texas program backed by up to $4.745B in CHIPS Act funding, offering US advanced-logic capacity contingent on reaching volume and customer qualification.

insights.claim: Samsung targeted November 2026 for construction start on Taylor Fab 2 in Texas, which will make 2-nanometer chips and aims to begin mass production in 2030.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Samsung's US 2nm capacity is a 2030 story — long-dated relative to competitors.

insights.claim: The Taylor fabs sit within a planned investment of more than $37 billion across Central Texas, including a Taylor R&D facility and Austin upgrades, supported by up to $4.745 billion in CHIPS Act direct funding to Samsung Austin Semiconductor.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: CHIPS subsidies anchor a large multi-fab US build-out by Samsung.

insights.claim: Samsung expects the two Taylor fabs to support roughly 3,500 direct jobs once both are operating.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Local workforce scale signals the size of the operation.

insights.claim: A second Taylor fab could give chip designers another US option for advanced logic such as AI accelerators and data center processors, adding geographic diversity, though the benefit depends on Samsung reaching volume production and customers qualifying designs.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Watch for named 2nm customer qualifications at Taylor as the real validation.
insights.quote: Those benefits depend on Samsung reaching volume production and customers qualifying their designs for the process.

insights.claim: Two production fabs plus an R&D facility could sustain Central Texas demand for equipment servicing, specialty materials and skilled technicians, building a regional semiconductor cluster over time.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Regional suppliers and service providers in Texas could benefit.
